title: The Past Hypothesis: why the early universe had low entropy
bottleneck: The second law of thermodynamics requires the universe to have started in an extraordinarily low-entropy state, with Penrose estimating the fine-tuning at one part in 10^10^123, yet no dynamical explanation for this initial condition exists. Inflation does not explain it; it assumes it.
why_it_blocks: The arrow of time itself, and with it all of thermodynamics, chemistry, and biology, depends on this unexplained initial condition; it is arguably the largest fine-tuning problem in physics.
current_state: Proposals range from eternal inflation's rare fluctuations to Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology, but none derives the low-entropy beginning from established physics. Penrose's Weyl curvature hypothesis proposes the initial singularity was special in a geometric sense, but it remains a conjecture without a dynamical mechanism.
